get.summary: Subscribe to the live domain-event stream.
get.description:
Every state change in the daemon — from HTTP calls, from the scheduler and
from agent activity alike — is published here. Each message carries a fresh
ULID `id`, the event kind as its `event` name, and the full updated DTO as
`data`, so clients patch their state without refetching.

Not every event is a database write. `task_branch_updated` is published by
the daemon's watch on each live task's branch ref, so a commit an agent
makes in its worktree — which changes nothing in the store — still says
that the task's diff (`GET /v1/tasks/{id}/diff`) is no longer the one you
hold. It carries the branch and the full sha of its new head.

There is **no replay or backfill**: the `id` is informational and
`Last-Event-ID` is ignored. On (re)connect, refetch the REST state you care
about and then follow the stream.

Besides the domain events there is a `heartbeat` event (a `HeartbeatDto`:
the daemon's `version` and its `started_at`), sent as the connection opens
and every 15 s an idle connection goes without one. It is a named event
rather than the SSE comment other streams keep alive with, because a
browser's `EventSource` never surfaces a comment: a client watches it to
tell a live daemon from a dead one, and a changed `started_at` to tell a
restarted daemon from the one it was talking to.

A client that falls too far behind loses events. It is never left silently
stale: the daemon sends a final `resync` event (`{"missed": n}`) and closes
the connection, so an `EventSource` reconnects and takes the refetch path
above.

parameters.name: goal
parameters.description: Only events belonging to this goal.

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: Only events belonging to this task.

200.description: SSE stream of domain events (text/event-stream). No replay on reconnect: refetch REST state first. A `heartbeat` event (HeartbeatDto) opens the connection and repeats every 15 idle seconds. A lagging client gets a final `resync` event (ResyncDto) and the connection is closed. `task_branch_updated` (TaskBranchDto) comes from the daemon's watch on the task branch rather than from a store write: it says a commit landed and the task's diff has moved.

Complete the goal: it moves active -> completed and every session of it
is torn down.
post.description:
The orchestrator's call, because it is the only agent that knows whether
the plan did what the goal asked for — the daemon can see that every task
ended, and not whether the goal is met. The user's too: it is their goal,
and a goal whose orchestrator will not start is otherwise one nothing can
close.

What the daemon checks is the part it can see. A goal with a task still
going is not one anybody may declare finished, however sure they are.

orchestrator's call alone, and there is nothing left for the user to
approve. A task with a column nobody staffs is refused by the column's
name: every task runs through every column, and one with nobody on it
would stop there.

get.summary: Daemon liveness probe.
Recent daemon log lines from the in-memory ring buffer, oldest first.

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description: Return only the last N lines.

get.summary: Follow the daemon log.
get.description:
The stream opens with a `snapshot` event carrying the current ring buffer
(a `LogSnapshotResponse`, what `GET /v1/logs` would have returned), then
sends a `delta` event per new line (a `LogLineDto`). Payloads are compact
JSON, so log content cannot break SSE framing. There is no replay on
reconnect: every connection starts over from a fresh snapshot, which is
also the resync path for a follower that fell behind and was dropped.

200.description: SSE stream of daemon log lines (text/event-stream). A `snapshot` event with the current buffer (LogSnapshotResponse), then a `delta` event per new line (LogLineDto). A follower that falls too far behind is disconnected; reconnecting starts over from a fresh snapshot.

get.summary:
Everything an agent can be pinned to, `<agent>:<model>` apiece: the
models discovery found each registry agent offering, grouped by agent.
No bare-agent entry: a model is required wherever an agent is pinned,
so there is nothing an agent on its own could be staffed as.
get.description:
Each entry carries the efforts it can be run at, as the agent offered
them, and which of them it runs by default. Every entry says whether
an agent can be staffed on it. A model the user turned off stays in
the list, off: a catalog that hid it would leave nothing to turn back
on, and nothing to say why a pin naming it is refused.

put.summary: Turn one entry of the catalog on or off.
put.description:
The catalog is discovery, so this writes only the exception:
an id nothing in the catalog carries is a 404, and the last entry left
on cannot be turned off — a plan needs something to be staffed on, and
a daemon that can staff nothing is not a state to leave a user in.

404.description: no such model in the catalog

409.description: it is the last model left enabled

put.summary: Set or clear a catalog entry's rank without changing its enabled flag.

404.description: no such model in the catalog

422.description: rank must be frontier, balanced, fast or local

install into: the download is minutes and gigabytes, and it would fail at
the end of them. Turning it off keeps every file on disk, so turning it
back on repairs its pinned package and weights.

parameters.name: task

parameters.name: requested
parameters.description:

for the ones that do not.

get.summary: One comment of a request Ariadne works on, read off the forge now.

post.summary:
Reply to one comment. The daemon posts the reply through the forge CLI,
marks it the review's where a review session posts it (029), and reads
the request again.

Resolve the thread of one comment, once a push fixed what it found
(029). Only a review session resolves, and only a thread it opened under
the integration login: the threads of anyone else stay open for the
person who wrote them.

get.summary:
The change under review, read in the reviewer session's worktree (029):
`git diff <base>...HEAD`, or `git diff <since>..HEAD` where `since` is
given. The base is the remote's copy of the base branch where the
checkout holds one, else the local branch.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Read the diff from this sha to the head, not from the base.

post.summary:
What the request's session says of it: `ready` once the babysitting task
believes every required approval and check reads green, on the head
(`head_sha`, required with `ready: true`) it actually confirmed that
against; and the head a review session posted its review on
(`reviewed_sha`). Neither raises `waiting_user` on the session by
itself (029): the claim alone is not confirmed evidence, and a
pr-reviewer session finishing its own review must notify nobody — the
`pull_request` attention producer reads the forge's own evidence
against this claim, for the head it names, and raises its own item
once it actually backs the claim up.

Post one round of a review of a request, in the user's name (029): its
new findings as one review of inline comments, each led by its priority,
and its summary, written into the one summary comment the review keeps
on the request — posted on the first round, edited on every later one. A
round with no new finding posts no review. `request_changes` stands only
on a P0 finding, new or still open. Any other event is refused, an
approval above all: the user gives every approval. What it posted is
marked as the review's.

One open request of a repository, read off the forge now (026): its

put.summary:
Ask Ariadne to review a request on the model the user picks, or stop
asking (029): a review session runs on that pin while the request is
open and out of draft. A request of the user's own posts each round as
a comment in the user's name; one that asks for the user's review on a
repository with no review pin of its own gets the manual start the
`pull_request` attention producer offers when nobody is assigned to it,
and posts as any other review Ariadne runs on it would (029). Asking
starts Ariadne's work on the request; stopping ends it, where no task
keeps the request. A request that asks for the user's review on a
repository that already pins one has a review already, and takes no
asking.

post.summary:
Start a loose session: a new conversation with an agent, in a directory,
with no goal, task or seat behind it.
post.description:
The model is checked as a goal's pin is — a registry agent and a model of
it, not one the user turned off — and the effort against that model. The
directory must be an absolute path to one that exists. The session comes
back live, waiting for the first prompt typed into its console, which
becomes its title.

get.summary: Inspect a session.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: session id

get.summary:
The session's newest events, in order: the transcript a console opens on.
It is a page of at most two hundred, the recent past rather than every
turn a session ever ran; `GET /v1/events` walks back from it. While a
turn runs, one `agent_thought_chunk` or `agent_message_chunk` holding the
text so far follows the stored events.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: session id

503.description: the console streamed faster than a snapshot could be read, every time it was tried; ask again

post.summary: Cancel the turn a session is running.
post.description:
Sends ACP `session/cancel` to the agent while its `session/prompt` is
still in flight. The turn then ends as any other does — the text so far
stored, then a `stop` whose `stop_reason` is `cancelled`. A session that
is not live, one whose agent process is gone, and one between turns all
have nothing to cancel, and say so with `409`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: session id

204.description: The running turn was told to cancel

post.summary: Type into a session.
post.description:
While a permission request is pending, the text selects that request's
option; otherwise it becomes a fresh `session/prompt` — sent at once if
the agent is between turns, or queued, in order, behind whichever one is
running and sent the moment it ends.

Both halves of "live" matter: the row's status, because a finished
session takes no more input, and the runtime itself, which has no agent to
hand a prompt to for a session whose process is gone.

And it is the user acting on the session, so whatever it was flagged for
comes down with the input: a permission answered, a question typed back,
a message read. An agent still blocked raises its own again with its next
event. The scheduler hears about it as it does about an ingested event, so
the quiet clock and the stream follow.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: session id

get.summary: Follow a session's console.
get.description:
Opens with a `snapshot` event carrying what `GET /console` would return —
the newest page of stored events, oldest first, then the running turn's
text so far — then an `event` per later one, each an `AgentEventDto`.
Subscribing happens before the snapshot is read and every later stored
event is compared against the snapshot's last id, so nothing committed in
between is ever missed or delivered twice; the live events are read under
the runtime's own turn lock for the same guarantee.

There is no replay and no `Last-Event-ID`: reconnecting starts again from a
fresh snapshot. A client that falls too far behind gets a final `resync`
event and the connection closes, exactly as `/v1/events/stream` does.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: session id

200.description: SSE stream of console events (text/event-stream). A `snapshot` event carrying the newest page of recorded events (`[AgentEventDto]`) and the running turn's text so far, then an `event` per new one (`AgentEventDto`) — message and thought chunks, tool call progress, tool calls, plans, permission requests and turn status all arrive this way, in the vocabulary the ACP runtime reports them in. The chunks and the progress are live only: they are never stored and never reach `/v1/events`. A client that falls behind gets a `resync` event (ResyncDto) and the connection closes.

get.summary: A session's console as a terminal.
get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket. The client sends JSON text frames — a `resize`
with the terminal's columns and rows first and on every change, a `key`
per key press and a `paste` per pasted text (`TerminalClientMessage`) —
and reads binary frames of terminal bytes that draw the console, plus a
text frame carrying the session's status as the socket opens and as it
ends (`TerminalServerMessage`). Closing the socket ends the console and
leaves the session running; the session ending, Ctrl-C twice or Ctrl-D
close the socket.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: session id

101.description: WebSocket. Client to server: JSON text frames, one `TerminalClientMessage` each — `resize` first, then `key` and `paste`. Server to client: binary frames of the terminal bytes that draw the console, and JSON text frames of `TerminalServerMessage`.

post.summary:
Revive an ended session: a new agent process, same agent conversation
(resumed via the stored internal session id). Returns the session to
attach to, which is this one either way — relaunched under its own id, or
untouched when its agent turned out to be alive already.
post.description:

post.description:

The daemon runs the forge call, never the agent: `gh` or `glab` only ever
run here, with the authentication the user already set up for them
([`crate::forge`]). The current column's agent supplies only what the
daemon cannot read off the task or the repository — the title and the
body — and gets the URL back to show the user.

One request per task: a task that already has a `pr_url` answers it again
and opens nothing, so a retried call never opens a second request.

with a column nobody staffs is refused by that column's name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: workflow name

AcpAgentDto.description: One ACP agent known to the daemon and its latest discovery result.

degraded.description: One flag for every optional capability that is absent.

id.description: Stable id used as the model-id prefix.

AcpAgentSource.description:
Where one registry entry came from: an agent of the ACP registry index
found on the daemon's `PATH`, or an `[[acp_agents]]` entry of its config.

AcpCapabilitiesDto.description: Required and optional ACP capabilities measured by discovery.

AcpDegradation.description: An optional ACP capability missing from an otherwise usable agent.

Actor.description: Who is attempting a transition: a seat, the daemon, or the user.

AgentAssignment.description:
One agent to staff on a task: the column it works, the skills it loads,
and what it is to run on.

The model is written `<agent>:<model>`: the id of an agent in the ACP
registry, and after the `:` one model of it. Both halves are required — a
model is required, and no agent default stands in for one — and a string
naming no registry agent is refused: nothing here derives one from the
other.

brief.description:
What to tell this agent beyond the task itself. Omitted = the task is
the whole of it.

effort.description:
The reasoning effort to run that model at, one of the efforts
`GET /v1/models` lists for it; anything else is refused. Omitted (or
"default") = whatever the agent runs the model at.

model.description:
What this agent runs on, `<agent>:<model>`. Required; the empty
string and the word "default" are refused.

skills.description:
The names of the skills this agent loads, in the order they reach it.
Omitted or empty = the column's own skills. A name no skill answers
to is refused.

step.description:
The id of the workflow column this agent works, one of the goal's
columns. A task takes one agent per column, and a column named twice
is refused.

AgentConfigDto.description:
How one registry agent is launched, shared by every session that runs on
it.

agent_id.description: The id of the agent in the ACP registry (`GET /v1/acp-agents`).

default_flags.description:
What Ariadne ships for this agent: what restoring the defaults writes
back — a client resets by sending these back as `extra_flags`. An ACP
agent ships with no flags, so this is empty.

extra_flags.description:
Argv flags appended to the agent's registry command on every spawn and
resume.

summary.description:
The one-line gist of `payload`, built by the daemon from the event's
own vocabulary rather than stored: an action and its subject for a tool
call, the agent's own words where it left any, and `…` where nothing
of it can be read.

AgentEventSummaryDto.description:
An agent event as the domain stream carries it: everything of
[`AgentEventDto`] but the payload, which reaches 1 MB. A client that wants
the payload reads `GET /v1/events`, or the console stream.

summary.description: The one-line gist of the payload, as [`AgentEventDto::summary`].

AgentUsageDto.description:
What one staffed agent spent on a task, named the way a reader addresses
it: an agent has no name of its own, so its column and its skills are what
identify it.

skills.description: The skills the agent loads; empty only if the agent is gone.

step.description:
The column the agent works; null for an agent the task no longer
staffs.

AiPermissionsState.description: Where the install has got to.

AiPermissionsStatusDto.description: The AI permission settings and the state of the install behind them.

allow_threshold.description: Danger at or below this value is allowed, 0 to 1.

deny_threshold.description: Danger at or above this value is denied, 0 to 1.

device.description:
The device the flavour runs on: the best one the machine could run it
on, unless another was chosen.

enabled.description: Whether the model answers permission requests at all.

endpoint.description: Where the model server answers, once one is running (022, Server).

flavour.description: The Kev flavour chosen, `4b` by default where the machine can run it.

flavours.description: Every flavour with every device it might run on, in wire order.

hardware.description: The machine the daemon runs on, probed afresh.

installed_release.description: The pinned model package and run on disk.

last_refresh_at.description: When the last install ended well, RFC 3339 in UTC.

latest_release.description: The pinned model package and run the last install used.

thresholds_default.description:
Whether the pair above is the default of the chosen flavour. `false`
where the user set it by hand; a flavour change then keeps it.

weights_present.description: Whether the checkpoints of the last good install are on disk.

AskReviewRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /v1/repositories/{id}/pull-requests/{number}/ariadne-review`:
whether Ariadne
reviews a request of the user's own (029).

effort.description: The effort that model runs at; none for the agent's own.

model.description:
The model the review runs on, `agent:model`: required to ask, and
checked against the catalog as any pin is.

skills.description:
The skills the review loads beside `pr-reviewer`, which every review
session loads; skills a task agent is staffed on.

AttentionCause.description:
What kind of blocker an item is, in the one vocabulary every producer
shares. `Unknown` is for a blocker a producer raises without reliable
evidence of which of the other four it is — it is never grouped with
another item, unknown or not (009, "Unknown causes remain separate").

AttentionInterventionsDto.description:
The times a person stepped in: permissions decided at the console,
questions and stalls. `person_secs` is how long those waited on the
person.

AttentionItemDto.description: One item on the Needs attention list.

affected.description:
Every entity this blocker's affected work names. A grouped item
(009, "A shared access or resource failure produces one grouped
item") lists every one of them here rather than splitting into an
item per entity.

id.description:
Stable across a restart and across the same cause recurring: derived
from the cause and what it shares rather than issued fresh, so the
same blocker is the same row for as long as it stands.

reason.description:
The shared contract's `reason`: why this blocker exists, in the one
vocabulary every producer draws from (`AttentionCause`).

required_action.description: The one action that clears this item.

since.description: When this blocker was first observed, RFC 3339.

summary.description: What is blocked and why, in one line.

AttentionListDto.description: The whole list, as `GET /v1/attention` answers it.

complete.description:
False where a producer's read failed, so a partial list is never
read as an all-clear: it still answers with whatever the other
producers found.

AttentionProducer.description:
Which producer raised an item — distinct from [`AttentionCause`], since
a cause describes *why* a blocker exists and a later producer (an
agent's own request, a pull request's next step) may share none of
recovery's causes, or raise `unknown` for a reason a client still needs
to tell apart from recovery's.

AttentionReason.description:
Why a live agent session needs the user's attention.

Orthogonal to [`SessionStatus`]: a session waiting on a permission prompt
is still `running` as far as its lifecycle goes, it just cannot make
progress until someone looks at it.

AttentionStatsDto.description: Response of `GET /v1/stats/attention`: how much did it need me?

AttentionSubjectDto.description: One entity an item's blocker affects.

label.description:
What to call it where there is room for one word more than the id —
a task's title, a session's model.

AttentionSubjectKind.description: What an item is about: an entity whose work the blocker touches.

oneOf.description: The console of the named session.
The named task.
The named pull request.
A settings section, named for the client's own routing.

AttentionTarget.description:
Where opening an item takes a client. Opening a target never resolves
the item on its own — only the thing the item names doing so does.

BinaryDto.description: A binary as the daemon can — or cannot — find it.

authenticated.description:
Whether it holds credentials for the service it speaks to, for the
binaries that hold any: `gh auth status` and `glab auth status`, asked
of the daemon's own environment because that is where the polling
runs. `None` for a binary with nothing to sign in to — git — and for
one that was not found to ask.

The distinction it exists for is the one that used to be invisible: a
`gh` that is installed and signed out answers every poll of a pull
request with a failure, and a task published to a forge is then
watched by nothing.

name.description: Executable name as it is looked up on PATH ("git", "gh").

path.description: Absolute path, when it was found.

version.description:
First line of its version output, when it answered in time. A binary
that is found but does not answer keeps its path and no version.

BucketDto.description:
The step a time axis is drawn at: a bar an hour over a very short span, a
bar a day over a short one, a bar a week over a long one.

CompleteGoalRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/goals/{id}/complete`: the orchestrator says the goal is
done. Its call, not the user's, and it carries nothing — every task being
finished or cancelled is the whole of the argument, and the daemon checks
that itself.

CompleteStepRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/step/complete`: the current column's agent
hands the task to the next column, or finishes it from the last one.

merge_commit.description: The commit the task landed as, which the `merged` gate checks.

reason.description: What the next column's agent is briefed with.

ConsoleInputRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/console/input`.

While a permission request is pending, the text selects that request's
option; otherwise it becomes a fresh `session/prompt`, sent at once or
queued behind the turn still running.

CreateAgentRequest.description: An explicit request from an agent for a human answer.

summary.description: The question or decision the human must answer.

effort.description:
The reasoning effort to run that model at, one of the efforts `GET
/v1/models` lists for it; anything else is refused. Omitted (or
"default") = whatever the agent runs the model at.

model.description:
What the orchestrator runs on, `<agent>:<model>` — the id of an agent
in the ACP registry and, after the `:`, the model of it:
`codex-acp:gpt-5.3-codex`, `opencode:ollama/llama3:8b`. Required —
a model is required, and no agent default stands in for one. The model
half is free text, handed to that agent as typed; a string naming no
registry agent is refused, and so are the empty string and the word
"default".

repository_ids.description: Ids of registered repositories (`POST /v1/repositories`); at least one.

workflow.description:
The workflow every task of the goal runs on, a name of the catalog
(`GET /v1/workflows`). Omitted = the default of the first repository.
It cannot change once the goal is created.

base_branch.description: Omit for the repo's currently checked-out branch.

default_workflow.description:
The workflow a new goal in this repository runs on where its request
names none. Omit for `develop-review-merge`.

oneOf.description: The forge integration to set up once the remote is detected.

path.description: Absolute path of an existing git work tree.

oneOf.description: Omit for `auto`.

document.description:
The whole `SKILL.md`, frontmatter included. A skill of the user's own
has no shipped text behind it, so it carries its own.

name.description: Kebab-case, and free: a name Ariadne already ships is refused.

agents.description:
The agents to staff: one per column of the goal's workflow, each with
its own model. A column left out is named when the plan is finalized.

depends_on.description: Task ids this task depends on.

repo_id.description:
Id of one of the goal's repositories; may be omitted when the goal
works in exactly one.

document.description:
The whole workflow document. Its `workflow <name>` line must equal
`name`.

name.description: Kebab-case, and free: a name Ariadne already ships is refused.

DaemonReportDto.description: The daemon's own environment, as `ariadne doctor` renders it.

acp_agents.description:
Every registry ACP agent and its cached discovery result: the agents
a session can be spawned on.

home.description: Home directory the daemon resolved, and the socket it listens on.

path.description: The daemon's `PATH`, the one every agent and git lookup uses.

python.description:
The Python interpreter the model's install runs on (022). It is reported
apart from `tools` because it answers a question of its own: not
whether it is there, but whether it is new enough.

tools.description:
The other binaries the daemon runs: git, without which no worktree can
be cut at all, and the forge CLIs `gh` and `glab`, which are what a
published task is watched through.

DeletedDto.description: Payload of the deletion events: the id of the gone entity.

DeviceOptionDto.description: Whether one device can run one flavour, and why not.

reason.description: Why it cannot, e.g. `needs 24 GB VRAM, found 8 GB`.

slow.description: A note only: the flavour can still be chosen on this device.

oneOf.description: Covers status changes: finalize, cancel, completion.

data.description: Covers status changes: finalize, cancel, completion.

oneOf.description: A terminal goal was deleted, its tasks with it.

data.description: A terminal goal was deleted, its tasks with it.

oneOf.description: Covers status transitions, edits, stall flags and worktree changes.

data.description: Covers status transitions, edits, stall flags and worktree changes.

oneOf.description:
Covers commits made in the task's worktree: the branch head moved, so
the task's diff against its base is no longer the one a client holds.

data.description:
Covers commits made in the task's worktree: the branch head moved, so
the task's diff against its base is no longer the one a client holds.

oneOf.description: One agent said something to another.

data.description: One agent said something to another.

oneOf.description: Covers status changes: kill, resume, exit, activity.

data.description: Covers status changes: kill, resume, exit, activity.

oneOf.description:
An agent event the ACP runtime recorded, without its payload: read the
whole event from `GET /v1/events`.

data.description:
An agent event the ACP runtime recorded, without its payload: read the
whole event from `GET /v1/events`.

oneOf.description: The AI permission settings or the state of its install moved (022).

data.description: The AI permission settings or the state of its install moved (022).

oneOf.description: The forge settings or the tunnel state moved (027).

data.description: The forge settings or the tunnel state moved (027).

oneOf.description:
The open issues of one repository moved on its forge (028): read them
again from `GET /v1/repositories/{id}/issues`.

data.description:
The open issues of one repository moved on its forge (028): read them
again from `GET /v1/repositories/{id}/issues`.

oneOf.description:
The requests of one repository moved: on its forge, or in what
Ariadne keeps of them (026). Read them again; they are the forge's.

data.description:
The requests of one repository moved: on its forge, or in what
Ariadne keeps of them (026). Read them again; they are the forge's.

EffortDto.description:
One reasoning effort an entry can be run at: the name it is passed by, and
what spending it buys.

At most one effort of a model is the `default`: what its agent runs it at
when a task pins no effort at all. None of them are where the agent has no
default to name.

default.description: Whether this is what the agent runs the model at when none is passed.

description.description:
What spending this effort buys, where the agent describes it. `null`
where nothing knows.

EventOrder.description: Which end of the recorded events a page of `GET /v1/events` is taken from.

FailStepRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/step/fail`: the current column's agent hands
the task back to the previous column, or fails it from the first one.

reason.description: What the previous column's agent is told to fix.

FailedCheckDto.description: One check that failed on a request's head.

conclusion.description:
The forge's own word for how it ended: `failure`, `cancelled` and
the like.

url.description: Where the forge shows the check's run; empty where it names none.

FinalizePlanRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/goals/{id}/finalize`: the orchestrator ends planning and
execution starts. The orchestrator's call, not the user's, and it carries
nothing — the plan is the tasks it wrote.

Flavour.description: A Kev flavour: how large a model to run.

FlavourOptionsDto.description: One flavour with every device it might run on.

ForgeDto.description: The forge a repository's remote is on, and whether Ariadne works with it.

login.description: The account the forge CLI is signed in as, stored on enable.

remote.description: The remote it was read off, `origin` where there is one.

review_model.description: The pin of the session that reviews a request; null starts none.

ForgeKind.description: The forge a repository's remote is on (025): which CLI speaks to it.

ForgeTunnelDto.description:
The forge settings and the tunnel state, as `GET /v1/forge/tunnel` and
`forge_settings_updated` carry them (027).

enabled.description: The switch: whether the daemon opens a tunnel.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, while the tunnel is down.

listen.description: The bound webhook listener address the tunnel forwards to.

since.description: When the tunnel entered its state.

url.description: The public URL while the tunnel is up.

ForgeUpdate.description:
A change to the forge integration; absent fields stay unchanged. A model
written empty clears that role's pin and its effort.

effort.description:
The reasoning effort that model is run at, pinned like `model`. None =
whatever the agent runs it at on its own.

model.description:
What the orchestrator runs on, `<agent>:<model>`: the registry agent
and, after the `:`, the model of it.

orchestrated.description: Whether this goal has an orchestrator for its lifetime.

repos.description:
The registered repositories the goal works in, as they stand now: a
goal references them, so an edit to one shows up here.

steps.description:
The columns of that workflow as they were when the goal was created:
a later edit of the catalog reaches later goals alone.

usage.description: What the agents of this goal have spent between them.

workflow.description:
The workflow every task of the goal runs on, chosen when the goal was
created.

GoalUsageDto.description:
What a goal cost, by the seat that spent it, and by the agent of every
column of every task under it.

agents.description:
One entry per agent of every task of the goal that has a session,
task by task and column by column.

orchestrator.description: The orchestrator's sessions, which belong to no task.

total.description: Every session of the goal summed, the orchestrator's included.

GpuDto.description: The GPU with the largest VRAM the daemon's probe found.

HardwareDto.description:
The machine the daemon runs on, as far as choosing a Kev flavour and
device cares.

status.description: Always "ok" when the daemon is able to answer.

HeartbeatDto.description:
Payload of the `heartbeat` control event.

Sent when a connection opens and on every idle interval afterwards, so a
client can tell a live daemon from a dead one without polling, and tell a
restarted daemon from the one it was talking to: `started_at` changes when
the daemon does.

started_at.description: When this daemon started, RFC 3339 in UTC.

version.description: The daemon's version, as `GET /v1/version` reports it.

IssuesChangedDto.description: Payload of `issues_changed`: the repository whose open issues moved.

LearnedPermissionDto.description:
One user choice or denial of an ACP permission request, keyed by the
repository, the tool name, the level and the normalized input.

family.description:
The command family of a `Bash` request, such as `git rebase`, else
the tool name.

key.description:
The kept fields of `rawInput` as compact JSON with sorted keys, its
one-time values replaced by placeholders such as `<HASH>`.

output.description: The model decision, when the model was called; null otherwise.

risk_tags.description:
The derived risk tags of the request. The row answers only a request
whose tags are all among them.

selected_option.description: The option id of the final choice.

target.description: The repository permission mode at the time of the decision.

tool_call.description: The ACP `toolCall`, its `rawInput` with sorted keys.

LearnedPermissionLevel.description: How much of a request a learned permission answers for.

LearnedPermissionTarget.description: The repository permission mode a learned permission was decided under.

level.description: Log level as tracing prints it.

message.description: Message followed by the event's fields as ` key=value` pairs.

target.description: Module path the event was emitted from.

ts.description: When the event was recorded, RFC 3339.

LogSnapshotResponse.description: Response of `GET /v1/logs`: the in-memory ring buffer, oldest first.

delivered_at.description:
When it was handed to the recipient's agent, or None while it is still
waiting for one to be free.

from_agent_id.description:
The staffed agent that sent it, or None for the orchestrator, the
daemon and the user.

task_id.description: The task it is about, or None for a message about the goal itself.

to_agent_id.description: The staffed agent it is for, or None for the orchestrator.

MessageKind.description:
What one agent is saying to another.

Agents talk to each other through one channel, and one kind carries
everything they say on it, whether it asks something or answers it. There
is no `answer` kind and no `reply` tool: an answer is a message to whoever
asked, addressed the way the question was, so nothing threads. Each
message reaches its agent as a turn — which is why the tool that sends one
takes questions and answers and nothing else, no confirmation and no
thanks.

A review used to run on the channel too, as three kinds of its own; a
workflow column moves a task through the step routes now, and the one
kind left is what the agents say.

ModelDto.description:
One thing an agent can be pinned to, as served by `GET /v1/models`: a
registry agent on a model discovery found it offering
(`claude-acp:claude-opus-5`). Every entry names both halves — there
is no bare-agent entry, because a model is required wherever an agent is
pinned.

The id is what a request writes as its `model`, whole. `agent_id` is its
registry prefix. Discovery supplies the description and efforts.
The user sets the enabled flag and optional rank independently.

description.description: One line about the model, which is what a picker shows beside the id.

efforts.description:
The reasoning efforts this entry can be run at, cheapest first; empty
where the model takes none, or where nothing knows what it takes.

enabled.description:
Whether an agent can be staffed on this entry. Every model is enabled
until the user turns it off; a disabled one stays in the catalog,
where it is shown as off and refused as a pin.

oneOf.description: The user-set rank, or `null` when the model is unranked.

ModelRank.description: A user-set rank, independent of discovery and model availability.

ModelSpendDto.description: What one model spent, every seat that ran on it pooled together.

share.description: `input_tokens + output_tokens` over the same total of every model.

ModelStatDto.description: What one model did in one seat.

goals.description: Distinct goals with a session of this model in this seat.

messages.description: The messages this model sent in this seat.

tasks.description: Distinct tasks with a session of this model in this seat.

tasks_finished.description: The tasks this model's column ended `finished`.

time_secs.description: The sum of the session lifetimes.

tokens.description: Input and output tokens of the ended sessions. Cached tokens are part of input.

NewSessionRequest.description:
Start a loose session: a new conversation with an agent, in a directory,
with no goal, task or seat behind it.

effort.description: The effort to run that model at; omitted = the agent's own.

model.description:
The model to run, `<agent>:<model>`: a registry agent (`GET
/v1/acp-agents`) and a model of it (`GET /v1/models`).

working_directory.description: The absolute path of an existing directory the agent works in.

OpenPullRequestRequest.description:
The agent of the `pr` column asking the daemon to open the pull or merge
request its task lands by. The daemon runs the forge's own CLI, so this
carries only what the agent cannot read off the task or the repository
itself.

body.description: Filled from the repository's own request template.

draft.description: Opens the request as a draft. Defaults to false.

title.description: Titled by the repository's own commit conventions.

ParsedWorkflowDto.description:
Response of `POST /v1/workflows/parse`: a document's name and columns,
read without saving it anywhere.

PathStateDto.description: A file or directory the daemon depends on.

writable.description:
Whether the daemon may write it, asked of the kernel (`access(2)`)
rather than inferred from the permission bits, which say nothing
about the user the daemon happens to run as. For a path that does not
exist yet this is its directory's answer: whether it could be created.
Nothing is written to find out.

PerFinishedTaskDto.description:
What a finished task spends, on average: the tokens of every session of a
task that finished, divided by how many tasks finished. 0 where none.

PermissionMode.description: How the ACP runtime answers a tool permission request.

PermissionReplyDto.description: The fields in a `permission.replied` event payload.

learned_id.description: The row that answered without a console choice.

learned_key.description: The normalized command key or family of the answering row.

PullRequestCommentDto.description:
One comment on a request, as the forge holds it now, read live (026),
with the marks Ariadne keeps of it.

answered.description: A later comment in the thread is by the integration login.

from_review.description: An Ariadne review session posted it (029).

id.description:
The forge's id of the comment, `rc-<n>`, `ic-<n>`, `rv-<n>` or
`note-<n>`: what `reply` and `resolve` take.

resolved.description: The forge reports the thread resolved.

thread_id.description:
The forge's thread or discussion; the conversation of the request
is one thread.

told_at.description: When the request's session was told of it.

PullRequestDto.description:
A pull request as the forge holds it now, read live (026), with what
Ariadne keeps of it where Ariadne works on it: the request a task opened,
one that asks for the user's review on a repository with a review pin,
or one of the user's they asked Ariadne to review.

behind_base.description: Whether the base branch has commits the head does not.

failed_checks.description: The checks that failed on the head, read as `unanswered_comments` is.

id.description:
Ariadne's id of the request while it works on it; null on a request
nobody works on, which the forge alone holds.

mergeable.description:
The forge's own mergeability for the head now: `clean`, `blocked`,
`dirty` or `unknown` where the forge has not finished computing it.

origin_task_id.description: The task that opened the request: its author keeps it (005).

ready.description: Whether the request's session reported it ready to merge.

review_asked.description:
Whether the user asked Ariadne to review this request of their own
(029).

review_model.description: The pin the user picked for that review.

review_requested.description: Whether the request asks for the user's review (029).

review_skills.description: The skills that review loads beside `pr-reviewer`.

role.description: `author` for a request of the user's, `reviewer` for any other.

session_id.description:
The newest session on this request, if any: its review session
(029), or the author of the task that opened it (005).

unanswered_comments.description:
The threads that wait on the user's login. Read where Ariadne works
on the request, or where the request is read on its own; 0 on a row
of a list nobody works on.

updated_at.description: When the forge last saw the request move.

PullRequestMatchDto.description: An open request a search found that is not the user's own.

PullRequestsChangedDto.description: Payload of `pull_requests_changed`: the repository whose requests moved.

PythonDto.description: The Python interpreter the daemon found, as it answered `--version`.

ok.description: Whether it is Python 3.12 or 3.13, which the model needs.

path.description: Absolute path, when one was found.

version.description: The version it printed, without the `Python ` in front of it.

ReportPullRequestRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/pull-requests/{id}/report`: what the request's session
says of it.

head_sha.description:
The head the session actually confirmed `ready` against — read off
its own last `get_pull_request` call, never looked up again here.
Required wherever `ready` is `true`: a push landing between that
read and this call must still be judged against the head the
session confirmed, not whatever the daemon's own cache has moved
on to since, or a push the session never actually saw could pass
as though it had (031).

ready.description: Every required approval and check reads green.

reviewed_sha.description: The head a reviewer session posted its review on (029).

default_workflow.description:
The workflow a new goal runs on where its request names none, a name
of the catalog (`GET /v1/workflows`).

oneOf.description:
The forge its remote is on, or null where the checkout has no usable
remote (025).

permission_mode.description:
How the ACP permission requests of every session in this checkout are
answered.

ResumeOutsideSessionRequest.description: Resume a stored conversation without a goal, task or seat.

ResyncDto.description:
Payload of the `resync` control event.

Sent as the last message of a connection that fell too far behind: the
daemon dropped `missed` events for it and closes the stream. The client
must refetch its REST state before following the stream again (an
`EventSource` reconnects on its own).

missed.description: Events this connection lost. Informational: they cannot be recovered.

ReviewCommentRequest.description: One inline comment of a review (029).

body.description: What goes wrong, and how to fix it.

line.description: The line in the new version of the file.

title.description: A short title of the defect; the comment opens on `[P0] Title`.

Seat.description:
Where an agent sits: the orchestrator of a goal, the agent of one workflow
column of a task, or the reviewer of a pull request (029).

A seat is a position, not an identity. Every agent below the orchestrator
is generic, and what it can do comes from the skills it loads; the seat is
only what the state machine and the launcher need to know about it.

SendMessageRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/messages` and `POST /v1/goals/{id}/messages`.

Who it is *from* comes from the session header rather than the body: an
agent cannot send a message as somebody else, and a message with no session
behind it is the user's.

to_actor.description: Who it is for. `orchestrator` needs no agent id — a goal has one.

to_agent_id.description:
The staffed agent it is for, as `GET /v1/tasks/{id}` lists them.
Required for `agent`, refused for the orchestrator.

oneOf.description:
Why this session needs the user's attention, if it does. Orthogonal to
`status`: an agent blocked on a permission prompt is still running.

attention_since.description: When the current `attention_reason` was first raised.

context_used.description:
The context window position the agent most recently reported. Both
fields stay null until the agent sends a `usage_update`.

effort.description:
Effort that model was launched at, off the same pin as `model`; null =
whatever the agent runs it at.

internal_session_id.description: The ACP agent's own session id.

model.description:
Model requested at launch, `<agent>:<model>`: the registry agent the
session runs on, and the model of it.

pull_request_id.description:
The pull request this session watches (026); null for every other
session.

switched_from.description:
The session this one replaced on its seat, when a switch started it
(`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/switch`); null otherwise.

task_agent_id.description: The staffed agent this session runs; None for an orchestrator or loose session.

task_id.description: None for an orchestrator or a loose session.

title.description:
A loose session's own title: the first prompt of the conversation it
resumed, or the first one typed into it. Null on a task's or a goal's
session, which goes by its work's title.

usage.description:
What this session's agent has spent, summed over every transcript it
reported under. Zeros while nothing has been reported.

worktree_path.description: The worktree, or the recorded working directory of a loose session.

SessionEntryDto.description:
One row of `GET /v1/sessions`: a session of either kind.

An outside conversation carries no goal, task, seat or status, because
Ariadne runs no work behind it; what it does carry is the agent it belongs
to, the id that agent loads it back by, where it ran and when it last did.

agent_id.description: The registry agent this conversation runs on (`GET /v1/acp-agents`).

created_at.description: When Ariadne created the row; None on an outside row.

effort.description: Effort that model was launched at, off the same pin as `model`.

id.description: Ariadne's session id, or the agent's own session id on an outside row.

internal_session_id.description: The ACP agent's own session id, which is `id` on an outside row.

last_activity_at.description: When this session was last active, which the page is ordered by.

model.description: Model requested at launch, `<agent>:<model>`; None on an outside row.

pull_request_id.description: The pull request this session watches; None for every other session.

oneOf.description: None on an outside row: Ariadne runs no process behind it.

task_agent_id.description:
The staffed agent this session runs; None for an orchestrator, a loose
session or an outside one.

title.description:
What this session is about: its task's title, the goal's title behind
an orchestrator, or the first prompt of an outside conversation.

oneOf.description: What this session's agent has spent; None on an outside row.

working_directory.description: The worktree, or the recorded working directory.

SessionKind.description:
Which half of the listing a row came from: a session Ariadne runs, or a
conversation an ACP agent stored that Ariadne did not start.

SessionPageDto.description: One page of `GET /v1/sessions`, newest activity first.

next_cursor.description: The `cursor` that continues after this page; null on the last one.

snapshot_at.description: When the outside snapshot this page was cut from was taken, RFC 3339.

total.description: How many sessions the filters leave, over every page.

SetModelEnabledRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /v1/models/enabled`: one model of the catalog, turned on or
off.

The id is a field rather than a path segment because a model id carries
`:` and often `/` (`opencode:anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`) — which is a
path of its own, not a segment of one.

SetModelRankRequest.description: Body of `PUT /v1/models/rank`. The id can contain colons and slashes.

oneOf.description: The new rank. `null` clears it.

SetTunnelRequest.description: `PUT /v1/forge/tunnel`: turn the tunnel on or off.

builtin.description:
Whether Ariadne ships this skill. A built-in is reset rather than
deleted; a skill of the user's own is deleted rather than reset.

document.description:
The whole `SKILL.md`: YAML frontmatter naming the skill and describing
it, then the body. This is the text set on the skill, or the one
Ariadne ships while a built-in has none of its own.

document_is_default.description: Whether `document` is the shipped text rather than one somebody wrote.

name.description: Kebab-case; how an agent loads the skill and how a task names it.

seat.description:
The seat this skill serves. An `orchestrator` skill cannot staff a
task agent.

summary.description:
The one line the skill says about itself, read off the `description`
of its frontmatter. It is what an agent sees before it opens the
document, and what a listing shows.

SkillSeat.description: Where a skill is used: by the orchestrator, or to staff a task agent.

SpendBucketDto.description: What was spent in one bucket of the time axis.

start.description: The RFC 3339 start of the bucket.

SpendStatsDto.description:
Response of `GET /v1/stats/spend`: what did it spend? Tokens over time, by
model, and per finished task — never a cost.

oneOf.description: The step `buckets` is drawn at.

buckets.description: One row per bucket from the first fact to the last, zeros included.

by_model.description: One row per model, every seat pooled, heaviest first.

SpendTotalsDto.description: Tokens spent across every ended session the filter keeps.

StepGate.description:
What a step waits for before the next one may start: the author's commit,
a push, a merge onto the base, or a request merged by a human.

SubmitReviewRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/pull-requests/{id}/reviews` (029): one review, posted
in the name of the integration login.

body.description:
The review's summary as it stands now: the daemon writes it into the
one summary comment the review keeps on the request.

event.description: `request_changes` or `comment`. Every other event is refused.

SwitchSessionRequest.description:
Switch a session to another model or agent: the old session ends, and a
new one starts on the same seat, on this pin, in a new conversation.

effort.description: The effort to run that model at; omitted = the agent's own.

model.description:
The model to run, `<agent>:<model>`: a registry agent (`GET
/v1/acp-agents`) and a model of it (`GET /v1/models`).

TaskAgentDto.description:
One agent staffed on a task: the column it works, what it knows, and what
it runs on.

The agent has no identity of its own. `step` says only which column of
the workflow it works; the skills are what it can do. What it runs on was
sized by the orchestrator when it staffed the task, or chosen by the user
since — either way it is what this agent runs on, and nothing behind it
changes that.

brief.description:
What the orchestrator told this agent beyond the task itself. None =
the task is the whole of it.

effort.description:
The reasoning effort that model is run at. None = whatever the agent
runs it at on its own.

session_id.description:
This agent's live session, the id `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/switch`
takes. None while it carries no live session.

skills.description: The skills this agent loads, in the order they reach it.

step.description: The id of the workflow column this agent works.

TaskBranchDto.description:
Payload of `task_branch_updated`: where a task's branch points now.

A commit in the task's worktree changes nothing in the store, so no
other event says the task's diff is no longer the one a client fetched.

branch.description: The task branch whose head moved.

head.description: Full sha of the commit the branch points at now.

agents.description:
The agents staffed on the task, one per column of its goal's
workflow, in the order the orchestrator listed them. What each one can
do is the skills it carries.

branch.description: The branch every column works on, in the one worktree the task has.

depends_on.description: Ids of tasks that must finish before this one starts.

merge_commit.description: The commit the task landed as, where its last column reported one.

pr_url.description:
URL of the pull or merge request the task's `pr` column opened, once
it has; null for a task landed directly.

reason.description:
Why a `failed` or `cancelled` task ended — an agent's own `fail_task`
reason, a dependency that never landed, a cancelled goal. Null for
every other status, and for an ending nobody gave a reason for.

repo_id.description: Id of the repository the task works in, one of its goal's.

stalled.description: Set when the agent went idle without advancing the task.

step.description:
The column of its goal's workflow the task is in while it is
`in_progress`; null before its first column and once it has ended.

usage.description: What the agents of this task have spent between them.

from_step.description: The column the task left, where the move crossed columns.

TaskUpdatedDto.description:
Payload of `task_updated`: the task as it now stands, plus the audit row
when the update was a status transition.

oneOf.description: Present when this update was a status transition.

TaskUsageDto.description:
What a task cost, by who spent it: one entry per agent that has a session
on the task, and the total of every session on it.

agents.description:
One entry per agent that has a session on the task, every run of it
summed, in column order. An agent whose session has yet to report
anything is listed with zeros; one that has never been spawned is not
listed at all.

total.description: Every session on the task summed, whatever its column.

TestAiPermissionRequest.description:
One permission request to score with the AI permission model, without
selecting an ACP option or recording an approval.

input.description: The raw JSON input the model sees in compact form.

kind.description: The tool call kind the model sees.

locations.description: The paths the tool call touches, as an agent sends them in `locations`.

options.description: The option names the model sees.

tool.description:
The tool call title the model sees, such as `git status` or
`Read /etc/hosts`, not the tool name.

workspace.description: The workspace used to derive whether a path is outside it.

TestAiPermissionResponse.description:
The AI permission model's score for a request, held to the current
thresholds.

ai_error.description: Why the model did not answer.

allow_threshold.description: Danger at or below this value is allowed.

cap.description: The first cap that changed an allow into an ask.

danger.description: The model's normalized danger score when it answered.

deny_threshold.description: Danger at or above this value is denied.

operation.description: The derived operation hint, when one is known.

probabilities.description: Kev's probabilities for the decision question.

risk_tags.description: The ordered risk tags derived from the complete request.

TimeStatsDto.description: Response of `GET /v1/stats/time`: how long does finished work take?

TokenUsageDto.description:
Tokens spent, as the agents' own transcripts report them.

Always present and always a number: nothing reported is zero, not null.

cached_input_tokens.description:
The subset of `input_tokens` served from the prompt cache, so never
added to it.

input_tokens.description: Prompt tokens, cache reads and cache writes included.

output_tokens.description: Completion tokens, thinking and reasoning included.

merge_commit.description:
The commit the task landed as, where `to` is `finished` and a column
reported one.

UpdateAgentConfigRequest.description: Body of `PUT /v1/agents/{id}`: the whole new flag list, empty included.

UpdateAiPermissionsRequest.description: Partial update of the AI permission settings; an absent field stays unchanged.

allow_threshold.description: Danger at or below this value is allowed. Values outside 0 to 1 are refused.

default_thresholds.description:
`true` drops a pair set by hand and goes back to the default pair of
the chosen flavour. Refused alongside either threshold.

deny_threshold.description: Danger at or above this value is denied. Values outside 0 to 1 are refused.

oneOf.description: A device with no flavour keeps the stored flavour.

enabled.description: Turning it on starts an install; turning it off keeps the files.

oneOf.description: A flavour with no device picks the best device that runs it.

UpdateLearnedPermissionRequest.description: Widen a row to every repository, or narrow it back to its own.

UpdateRepositoryRequest.description: Partial update; absent fields stay unchanged.

description.description: New description, or empty to clear it. Absent = unchanged.

oneOf.description: Absent = unchanged.
Absent = unchanged.

UpdateSkillRequest.description: Partial update; absent fields stay unchanged.

document.description:
The new document. Absent = unchanged; putting a built-in back on the
text Ariadne ships is `POST /v1/skills/{name}/document/reset`.

UpdateTaskRequest.description: Partial update; only allowed while the task is pending, ready or failed.

agents.description:
The whole staffing, replaced: every column is staffed afresh, with
the skills and the model it names. The way to staff a column a task
lacks before it is retried.

UpdateWorkflowRequest.description: Partial update; absent fields stay unchanged.

document.description:
The new document. Absent = unchanged; putting a built-in back on the
text Ariadne ships is `POST /v1/workflows/{name}/reset`.

WebhookDto.description: Public hook status. The hook secret is never serialized.

fetch_error.description:
Why the last fetch of the repository's requests failed, or null once
one works: what says polling works, where no hook is live.

WorkBucketDto.description: One bucket of the time axis: the counts of the facts that fall in it.

start.description: The RFC 3339 start of the bucket.

bucket.description:
`"hour"`, `"day"` or `"week"`: the bucket every
[`WorkBucketDto::start`] falls on.

buckets.description: One row per bucket from the first fact to the last, zeros included.

WorkTotalsDto.description: The counts `WorkStatsDto` answers over the whole span a filter keeps.

finish_rate.description: `tasks_finished` over the three endings; 0 where there are none.

builtin.description:
Whether Ariadne ships this workflow. A built-in is reset rather than
deleted; a workflow of the user's own is deleted rather than reset.

document.description: The effective document: the override, or the text Ariadne ships.

name.description: Kebab-case; named on the document's first line.

oneOf.description:
What the step waits for before the next one starts, where the
document named one.
The model rank the step prefers, where the document named one.

skills.description: The skills an agent on this step loads.
